paper_abstract: Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 positions media as both an instrument and an object of national transformation. This systematic literature review synthesizes peer-reviewed evidence published between January 2016 and September 2026 to establish how, and under what conditions, media contribute to social change. In accordance with PRISMA 2020, a search of Open Alex conducted on September 28, 2026, was complemented by scoping searches; 86 studies in journals indexed in Scopus or the Directory of Open Access Journals were appraised on design features adapted from the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool and synthesized thematically across three mechanisms: ownership and investment, digital audience engagement, and regulation. Three convergent patterns emerge. State-led investment and cultural policy have expanded capacity and youth-oriented production across television, film, streaming, gaming, and entertainment, a pattern termed here managed diversification. Platforms have become arenas in which reform, particularly women’s empowerment and flagship national projects, is debated, endorsed, and normalized, with influencers as prominent intermediaries. Regulatory modernization has formalized a fast-growing creator economy, and women’s professional inclusion has advanced, while studies report reliance on official sources and link legal uncertainty and perceived monitoring to anticipatory self-restraint. The review refines the concept of conditional transformation: the communicative visibility of reform has expanded substantially at home and abroad, whereas editorial autonomy has expanded more gradually, and the evidence points to regulatory predictability as a condition for its further expansion. The review maps gaps in political-economy, longitudinal, and reception research and derives recommendations aligned with Vision 2030’s commitment to effective, transparent, and accountable government.

paper_title: Short-Term Mobility Gains and Unmeasured Longer-Term Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Home-Based Posterior Shoulder Stretching for Glenohumeral Internal Rotation Deficit and Posterior Shoulder Tightness in Active Populations
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Posterior shoulder stretching is widely prescribed for gleno-humeral internal rotation deficit (GIRD) and posterior shoulder tightness (PST), but durability of benefit and adherence to home programmes are poorly reported. This review evaluated the outcomes and adherence of home-based posterior shoulder stretching programmes in active populations, with pre-specified emphasis on outcomes measured beyond the immediate post-intervention period. Methods: Nine electronic sources, including ClinicalTrials.gov, were searched. Eligible studies were controlled interventions of primarily home-based posterior shoulder stretching in adolescents or adults with GIRD and/or PST. Screening and extraction were performed in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty using GRADE. Continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models with mean differences or standardised mean differences. Results: Of 1,228 records, 70 full texts were assessed and nine studies (361 randomised participants) were included. Compared with no stretching or usual activity, stretching increased internal rotation by 13.91° (95% CI 2.61–25.22; two studies, 99 participants; I² = 94%; very low certainty) and horizontal adduction (standardised mean difference 1.20, 95% CI 0.77–1.63; two studies, 99 participants; I² = 0%; low certainty). Sleeper and cross-body stretches did not differ (−0.16°, 95% CI −9.83–9.50; two studies, 53 participants). Five studies reported adherence using five different formats. Conclusions: Low- to very-low-certainty evidence suggests that home-based posterior shoulder stretching may improve shoulder mobility over three to eight weeks, without demonstrated superiority of one technique. No included study provided a post-intervention comparison capable of determining whether stretching-related mobility gains were retained; therefore, durability remains uncertain.

paper_title: <span data-teams="true">Behavioral and Neurobiological Outcomes in the Reserpine-Induced Fibromyalgia-Like Model in Rodents: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Background: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a chronic nociplastic pain condition characterized by widespread pain and non-nociceptive symptoms. The reserpine-induced model is widely used to investigate FM-like phenotypes in rodents, but methodological heterogeneity may affect phenotype expression and reproducibility. Objective: This scoping review intended to identify published research that involved behavioral and neurobiological outcomes of reserpine-induced FM-like conditions and identify factors underlying phenotypic varia-bility. Design: Four databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus) were as-sessed. The search strategy was not restricted by publication date. Eligible studies were experimental studies in rats or mice using reserpine-based protocols and reporting affec-tive, cognitive, or neurobiological outcomes. Study selection and data extraction were in-dependently performed by two reviewers, and methodological quality was assessed using SYRCLE. Results: This review shows that a study heterogeneity is further increased by species, strain, sex, reserpine dose and administration regimen, vehicle composition, out-come assessment timing, and experimental settings. Thus, these aspects should be ad-dressed while interpreting and comparing test data. In rodent research, the most consist-ently observed characteristic is the emergence of long-term mechanical and deep-tissue hypersensitivity, accompanied by converging alterations in monoaminergic modulation, neuroimmune and inflammatory signaling, spinal and supraspinal excitability, and pe-ripheral metabolic and oxidative functions. This alignment of behavioral, neurochemical, electrophysiological, histological, and peripheral results offers biological validity to the paradigm, expanding outside simply inducing nociceptive hypersensitivity. Conclusions: Using reserpine to evaluate fibromyalgia-associated pain biology is useful and mechanis-tically relevant. Behavioral, neurochemical, electrophysiological, histological, and periph-eral data support the paradigm beyond nociceptive hypersensitivity.
paper_authors: Edilaine Rosa Acosta dos Santos Moreira

paper_title: Neuroprotective Effects and Mechanisms of Cannabinoids in In Vitro Cell Models of Neurodegenerative Diseases: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), Huntington's disease (HD), and multiple sclerosis (MS) collectively affect millions of people worldwide, and none currently has a disease-modifying pharmacotherapy. Natural, semisynthetic, and synthetic cannabinoids have shown neuroprotective activity in preclinical models, but most remain at an early experimental stage, and their mechanisms of action have not been systematically mapped across disease contexts. Objective: This scoping review maps the preclinical evidence predominantly in vitro, with select studies incorporating in vivo validation on exogenous cannabinoids, including phytocannabinoids, synthetic cannabinoid receptor agonists, and cannabinoid-active phytochemicals (e.g., β-amyrin), and their neuroprotective mechanisms across cellular models of AD, PD, HD, and MS. Methods: This review followed JBI methodological guidance, and PRISMA-ScR reporting standards, with a protocol prospectively registered on OSF (10.17605/OSF.IO/TAQ9F). PubMed, MEDLINE, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Web of Science were searched, yielding 8,484 records (2,844 after deduplication). Following two-stage screening in Rayyan, 194 reports were sought for full-text retrieval; 176 were assessed for eligibility, and 26 preclinical studies (2015-2025) met the inclusion criteria. Results: Most included studies were purely in vitro (n = 18); six combined in vitro and in vivo methods, and two used in vitro and in silico or ex vivo components. Studies addressed AD (n = 12), PD (n = 8), general neuroinflammation models (n = 3), HD (n = 2), and MS (n = 1). Cannabidiol (CBD) was the most studied compound (n = 9), followed by the synthetic agonists JWH-133 and ACEA (n = 6 combined), THC and its analogues (n = 5), and WIN 55,212-2 (n = 4). Evidence converged on three mechanistic domains: (1) anti-neuroinflammatory signaling in microglia and astrocytes; (2) antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, and mitochondrial pathways; and (3) protein aggregate clearance, autophagy, myelination, and neurotransmitter modulation. Receptor pharmacology spanning canonical CB1R/CB2R signaling, non-canonical receptors (PPARγ, GPR55, A2AR, TRPV1), and receptor heteromerization emerged as a cross-cutting axis linking these domains rather than a fourth, parallel mechanism. Conclusion: Cannabinoid-mediated neuroprotection in AD, PD, HD and MS cannot be explained by canonical receptor pharmacology alone; formulation effects and off-target, receptor-independent mechanisms account for a substantial share of the reported activity. Priorities for translation include systematic dose-response characterization, development of CNS-penetrating CB2R agonists, and target-deconvolution studies to establish how prevalent receptor-independent mechanisms/ direct molecular are.

paper_title: Beyond Carbon: Towards a Social Lifecycle Assessment Framework for Green Façades and Green Roofs in Sustainable Building Design: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Green facades and green roofs are increasingly promoted as core strategies for building decarbonisation, energy-efficient design, and ecological building concepts, with their environmental performance extensively documented through Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). However, the social dimension of these interventions occupant wellbeing, labour conditions embedded in the production of renewable and recycled materials, equity of access to green retrofits, and community acceptance remains largely absent from mainstream sustainability assessment. This paper conducts a systematic review, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, of the LCA literature on green roofs and living walls published between 2015 and 2025, screening 264 records identified in Scopus and Web of Science down to 45 included studies. The review finds that environmental, economic, and technical performance evaluations dominate this literature, and that the evidence base is heavily concentrated on green roofs (91% of included studies) rather than green facades or living walls (9%). Only one included study applies a full Social Lifecycle Assessment (S-LCA) methodology to a green roof, confirming that social sustainability evaluation of vegetated building envelopes exists but remains an isolated, non-cumulative contribution rather than an established practice. Drawing on the identified findings, this paper develops a preliminary S-LCA framework for green roofs and living walls, modifying the five UNEP/SETAC stakeholder categories to better reflect the specific characteristics and social implications of vegetated envelopes. The framework provides a more comprehensive approach for researchers and policy-makers to assess the broader impacts of building greening strategies beyond conventional environmental performance indicators.

paper_title: Bridging Model Sophistication and Managerial Adoption: A Structured Review of Operations Research in FMCG Supply Chain Optimisation
paper_abstract: Operations research (OR) has long supported supply chain decisions for fast moving consumer goods (FMCG), a sector marked by thin margins, short shelf lives, demand that swings with promotions and highly fragmented retail. This review examines whether OR models capture these features and whether richer models reach practice. We analyse 22 peer reviewed applications published between 1994 and 2024, coding each model against seven defining characteristics of FMCG to form an FMCG Specificity Index, and against a four level scale of adoption evidence. Nineteen of the 22 models extend the classical transportation problem. Mean specificity is low, at 2.09 out of 7: promotions are modelled in one study and demand uncertainty in four. Adoption evidence is not significantly related to specificity (Spearman ρ = −0.21, p = 0.36) but tends to decline as solution methods grow more complex (ρ = −0.37, p = 0.12). All five implemented models rely on exact methods or constructive heuristics, whereas none of the six metaheuristic models reports implementation. We therefore propose simplicity preserving specificity as a design principle and demonstrate it with real promotion data from a US grocery retailer. The resulting FMCG Fractile Method can be applied in a spreadsheet, matches the optimal stochastic plan to within 0.005 percent of expected cost, and reduces expected cost by 13 to 57 percent relative to planning that ignores promotions. The review closes with a research agenda and a reporting checklist for FMCG optimisation studies.

paper_title: Physical Activity Promotion in Primary Diabetes Care: A National Survey of Nurses in Bahrain
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Physical activity is an important component of type 2 diabetes (T2DM) management, and nurses are well-positioned to promote it in routine care. However, little is known about its implementation by diabetes nurses working in primary healthcare in Bahrain. This study examined nurses’ perceptions, confidence, knowledge, awareness, guideline awareness and use, promotion practices, and perceived barriers to physical activity. Methods: A national cross-sectional mixed methods study was conducted among primary healthcare nurses. All 52 eligible nurses were invited to participate, with 49 completing an online questionnaire. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive and exploratory statistics, and free-text responses using inductive thematic analysis. Results: Nurses strongly perceived physical activity promotion to be part of their professional role and reported high confidence in providing advice. However, 44.9% were aware of at least one physical activity guideline and 24.4% reported both awareness and routine use. Only 34.7% reported always assessing patients’ physical activity irrespective of presenting health needs. Nurses reported that the most commonly perceived barriers among people in Bahrain were lack of time (83.7%) and lack of motivation and support from family and friends (67.3%). Qualitative findings identified four themes: public awareness and health education; access to physical activity facilities and opportunities; motivation and behavioural support; and healthcare and community support. Conclusions: Diabetes nurses in Bahrain demonstrated a strong professional commitment to promoting physical activity, but this was not consistently reflected in systematic, guideline-informed practice. Greater awareness and implementation of existing guidance, practical approaches to physical activity assessment, clearer referral pathways, and coordinated healthcare and community support may strengthen physical activity promotion.

paper_title: A Systematic, Taxonomy-Guided Survey of Predictive Maintenance in Robotic Systems: Fault Detection, Diagnosis, Prognosis, and Fault-Tolerant Control
paper_abstract: Robotic systems have become critical assets across manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, and field operations, yet their maintenance remains fragmented across a literature that treats sensing, actuation, mechanical wear, and system-level failure as unrelated topics rather than facets of a single problem. This survey addresses that fragmentation by organizing robot fault detection, diagnosis, prognosis, and fault-tolerant control around a unified four-category taxonomy, sensor, actuator, mechanical, and system-level faults, applied consistently across eight robot platforms: industrial robotic arms, wheeled mobile robots, legged robots, collaborative robots, aerial robots, surgical robots, underwater robots, and humanoid robots. Following a PRISMA-inspired screening process across four databases (IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, Scopus, and ScienceDirect) covering publications from 2022 to 2026, an initial pool of approximately 1,800 identified records was narrowed through duplicate removal, title and abstract screening, and full-text eligibility assessment to 115 studies meeting this survey's inclusion criteria. Within this literature, industrial robotic arms account for the largest share of coverage, while acoustic emission sensing, optical and fiber Bragg grating sensing, communication-layer system faults, and humanoid-specific fault detection are addressed by a comparatively small number of studies despite the same search effort applied uniformly across every category. Methods are reviewed independently of fault category, spanning classical machine learning, deep learning architectures including recurrent, convolutional, state-space, and generative models, graph neural networks, federated learning, hybrid approaches, and model-based probabilistic methods. Recurring challenges are identified across the reviewed literature, including data scarcity relative to normal operating hours, heterogeneous data across robot fleets, domain shift between laboratory and deployment conditions, sensor corruption under real-world noise, real-time feasibility on constrained onboard hardware, and platform-specific limitations most pronounced for humanoid, surgical, and underwater robots. This survey does not propose new fault-detection algorithms; its contribution is the taxonomy itself and the structured synthesis of existing methods against it, together with a research agenda mapping identified challenges to near-term, mid-term, and long-term directions for the field.

paper_title: The 2023 Emilia-Romagna Geo-Hydrological Disaster: Critical Decision-Making Issues Identified by Literature Review
paper_abstract: In May 2023, the Emilia-Romagna region (northern Italy) was hit by two unexpected extreme weather events that caused 17 deaths, the displacing of 50,000 people, and damages amounting to over 10 billion euros. Such a geo-hydrological disaster has stimulated scientific investigation, and tens of papers have been published. In this review, peer-reviewed publications are examined with the aim of identifying critical issues relevant to the decision-making process. These questions are crucial for policy makers and territorial government agencies, who play a direct and fundamental role in disaster management. The review was performed in accordance with the PRISMA method and by the citation and indexing databases of Scopus and Web of Science (WoS). Its main findings are summarized as follows: (1) in flood and landslide mitigation, land-use planning adequate to the climate-adjusted scenarios must be designed and implemented; (2) early warning systems should be people-centered and based on more advanced weather forecasts or new methods, like the elaboration of cellular geo-referenced data; (3) the use of integrated approaches based on machine learning and other modern technologies is increasing being proposed to improve performance in disaster response. It can be concluded that the reviewed literature informs policy for improving government guidelines, rules, and decision-making in disaster management.

paper_title: Development Status and Future Directions of Unmanned Surface Vehicles in Marine Geological Surveying
paper_abstract: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) have emerged as a new type of marine carrier platform and are attracting increasing attention in marine geological surveying owing to their flexibility, low observability and unmanned operation. This review systematically traces the development history and current status of USVs worldwide and in China, and summarizes the state of the art of USV-based marine geological survey technology from three perspectives: autonomous control, sensor integration, and data transmission and processing. Two representative applications, seafloor topographic and geomorphological surveying and sub-seafloor geophysical exploration, are examined to illustrate engineering practice. Recent advances and technological trends are then outlined in terms of cross-domain collaborative operations, upgrading of core equipment, expansion of application scenarios and standardization. Remaining challenges are analyzed, including limited adaptability to complex environments, insufficient autonomous decision-making, data quality control and the low domestic production rate of core components, and future development directions are proposed. With continued technological progress, deeper research and improvement of the relevant survey standards, USVs are expected to mature into a stand-alone technical means for marine geological surveying.

paper_title: A Systematic Review of Post-Quantum Cryptography: Challenges, Research Gaps, and Future Research Directions
paper_abstract: Quantum computers threaten to break asymmetric cryptography protocols almost immediately. To address this, researchers are developing post-quantum cryptography (PQC), which offers greater security but comes with higher costs and greater implementation complexity. The objective of this article is to identify the NEW cryptographic schemes, methods, and algorithms designed to resist quantum attacks. To do so, we first conducted a literature review that included mapped studies, systematic reviews, and surveys published in 2025 and mid-2026. This would help identify gaps and knowledge vacuums. Second, we conducted a systematic review using the PRISMA methodological guidelines for the period between 2020 and mid-2026 to compare the performance of PQC schemes, characterize the main challenges of their implementation, and identify trends. The results show that lattice-based schemes, followed by code-based and hash-based schemes, are the most extensively researched because they balance security, computational efficiency, and readiness for standardization. Furthermore, the most commonly reported performance metrics are key and signature sizes, as well as execution times. Meanwhile, scalability, power consumption, and performance on resource-constrained devices have been explored very little. Our study concludes with the key priorities that are likely to shape the future development of PQC.

paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Pharmaceutical Water: A Comprehensive Review of Contamination, Biofilm Formation, Antimicrobial Resistance, Detection, and Mitigation
paper_abstract: The opportunistic pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a flexible Gram-negative bacterium with inherent antibiotic resistance, remarkable ability to create biofilms in environments of limited nutrients and water, and a significant armory of virulence factors that makes it one of the most important opportunistic pathogens in hospitals and pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities. Water for pharmaceutical use is employed as both an ingredient, a process medium, and a cleaning material during the manufacture of drugs; thus, pharmaceutical water presents P. aeruginosa with perfect conditions (warm temperature, low nutrients, high surface-to-volume ratio, and constant circulation). This review discusses peer-reviewed, freely available scientific publications about biology, antibiotic resistance, prevalence, and control of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in pharmaceutical water supplies and in the cosmetics product chain where contamination with waterborne pathogens has been associated with recalls in the European Union and elsewhere. According to the U.S. Pharmacopoeia, P. aeruginosa is required to be absent in purified water and non-sterile water-based products. The rapid alert system of the European Union identifies Pseudomonas aeruginosa as the most frequently isolated microorganism from microbiologically contaminated cosmetics. Hospital-acquired infections have been associated with biofilm contamination of faucet aerators, sink traps, solenoid diaphragms, and electronic-eye faucets in various scenarios, including neonatal ICU outbreaks and adult ICU outbreaks that have yielded carbapenemase-producing lineages. Prevention measures should entail multiple approaches including water pretreatment, periodic hot water (≥65–70 °C) or steam sanitization, ozone or peracetic acid-UV sanitization, hypochlorous acid flushing, 0.2-µm filters, and continuous monitoring with culture (USP <60>, <61>, <62>) and rapid molecular (real-time PCR of gyrB or gyrA) tests. Overall, all the above can bring down water system bioburden from “uncountable” to <0.1 × 10¹ CFU/mL.

paper_title: Comparative Review of Provenance and Attribution Architectures for AI-Generated Multimedia Under Adversarial and Operational Stress Conditions
paper_abstract: As generative AI (GAI) becomes more accessible and popular, AI-generated multimedia (images, videos, audio, deepfakes) is proliferating. The developments have increased the urgency of issues such as media authentication, provenance, responsibility, and abuse in digital environments. While state-of-the-art solutions are good at detecting if the content is generated or altered by an AI, they do not aim at identifying the source, history, or long-term attribution of an item. Recent work proposes different types of provenance and attribution systems based on cryptographic signatures, watermarks, generator attribution, third-party registries, and governance models. This article reviews existing provenance and attribution architecture approaches for AI-generated multimedia in decentralized GAI environments. It introduces a taxonomy based on literature surveys, and a literature-inspired comparison framework that helps categorize existing approaches and compare their advantages and disadvantages in terms of different scenarios (including metadata stripping, compression/transcoding, screenshots, redistribution, AI-to-AI regeneration, model updates). Provenance architectures assume that (a) metadata can be preserved, (b) the signal can be traced, (c) the model will remain stable, (d) content records will survive, and (e) that systems will cooperate. In a decentralized environment, these assumptions can quickly disappear, making them weak points. AI-to-AI regeneration represents a significant challenge to continuous attribution for all analyzed categories. Finally, it implies that hybrid provenance architectures could be a way forward since they associate different provenance/attribution mechanisms; nevertheless, the few available ones are still limited because of interoperability, system participation, coverage, complexity, and robustness.

paper_title: From Sensors to Twins: A Review of Medical Digital Twins Across Physiological Systems and Their Path to Real-Time Deployment
paper_abstract: A medical digital twin (MDT) is a patient-specific computational model that stays linked to the patient through incoming data from wearable and clinical sensors, and feeds its predictions back into care. Most current MDTs are built and run offline, yet their usefulness depends on continuous data from wearables and clinical sensors. This review looks at MDTs through that lens across four physiological systems: nervous, hepatic, endocrine, and immune. For each, we describe how mechanistic, data-driven, and hybrid models are used, and how calibration, validation, and uncertainty quantification turn a generic model into a patient-specific one. The endocrine system is the most mature case. Twins built on continuous glucose monitoring already support insulin dosing decisions and artificial pancreas testing. We then consider what it would take to run MDTs closer to the patient: surrogate models that replace costly simulations, compressed deep learning models, and inference on wearable or mobile devices. The main obstacles are scarce data, weak generalization across populations, computational cost, the difficulty of linking multiple organ models, and limited clinical evidence. We close with a roadmap for clinicians, modelers, and engineers working together.

paper_title: Detection and Decision-Making for Secondary Caries: A Scoping Review Informing a Clinical Decision Framework
paper_abstract: Background: Secondary caries or caries around restorations or sealants is a common reason for replacement of restorations. However, distinguishing true secondary caries from restoration-related defects remains clinically difficult and may lead to overtreatment and unnecessary removal of healthy tooth structure. Objectives: This scoping review aimed to map how diagnostic strategies for secondary caries are used and how these findings are translated into treatment decisions, while identifying diagnostic thresholds and informing an evidence-based decision framework. Methods: Searches were performed in seven electronic databases, gray literature sources, and guideline repositories without restrictions on language or publication year. Evidence addressing diagnostic strategies for secondary caries, as well as relevant guidelines and consensus documents, were included. Data were organized descriptively, and the methodological quality of primary studies was critically evaluated. Results: Forty-eight documents were included (34 original studies and 14 guidelines or consensus statements). Visual–tactile examination, commonly combined with bitewings, was the most frequently reported detection approach. Adjunctive methods, including fluorescence-based devices, optical imaging, and artificial intelligence, were investigated as complementary detection tools, with heterogeneous performance across study designs. Treatment decisions were primarily driven by lesion activity and suspected dentine involvement rather than marginal appearance alone. Explicit diagnostic thresholds were rarely predefined, and substantial variability was observed in how diagnostic findings informed treatment decisions. Conclusions: The evidence supports visual–tactile assessment complemented by bitewings as first-line approaches within a diagnostic strategy for secondary caries evaluation. However, heterogeneity in diagnostic thresholds and treatment decision criteria limits comparability across studies and may contribute to inconsistent clinical management. Greater standardization in reporting diagnostic strategies and decision frameworks is needed to support evidence-based and conservative care. Clinical significance: This review provides an evidence-informed clinical framework based on visual–tactile and radiographic assessment for secondary caries around restorations. By integrating detection methods, lesion interpretation, and commonly reported clinical thresholds, the framework illustrates how findings from routine assessment are translated into treatment strategies. The findings indicate that treatment decisions are more consistently guided by lesion activity and dentine involvement than by restoration defects alone, supporting a more conservative approach under diagnostic uncertainty and highlighting the need for greater standardization in clinical criteria.

paper_title: Too Few, Too Far: Can AI Agents Address Health Workforce Shortage in Poland and Maldistribution in China? A Comparative Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background: Health workforce strain undermines care delivery worldwide, but its structure differs by country: Poland faces an absolute shortage of doctors and nurses, while China faces geographic maldistribution of an otherwise adequate physician supply. Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly proposed as a partial remedy for both. Objectives: This review compares AI agent adoption in Chinese and Polish healthcare against each country’s workforce mechanism, using the Non-adoption, Abandonment, Scale-up, Spread and Sustainability (NASSS) framework. Methods: A narrative review followed the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) checklist, given a heterogeneous, fast-evolving evidence base spanning peer-reviewed studies, preprints, and institutional reports; databases and preprint servers were searched for AI agents deployed or piloted in China and Poland since 2020. Results: Chinese cases span rule-based and LLM triage systems, clinical decision-support tools, a retrieval-augmented specialty LLM for ophthalmology, an autonomous multi-agent hospital simulation, and nationwide DeepSeek-R1 primary-care deployment; Polish cases span virtual triage engines, EMR-embedded decision-support, a diagnosis-prediction model, and ambient documentation scribes. Chinese agents redistribute capacity; Polish agents relieve clinical and documentation workload. Conclusions: AI agent adoption plausibly tracks each country’s workforce mechanism, but evidence for genuine labor substitution, rather than efficiency gains, remains limited.

paper_title: Complication, Technical Pitfalls, and Strategies for Reducing Donor-Site Morbidity Following Connective Tissue Graft Harvesting: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Connective tissue grafts (CTGs) remain a vital component in periodontal and pe-ri-implant plastic surgery; however, their harvesting creates a second surgical wound at the palatal donor site. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence on com-plications, technical pitfalls, and strategies for reducing donor-site morbidity following the harvesting of subepithelial connective tissue grafts and de-epithelialized gingival grafts. Subepithelial harvesting techniques support primary wound closure but require adequate residual flap thickness and careful dissection. In contrast, harvesting de-epithelialized gingival graft creates an open wound that demands effective hemostasis and protection; however, this approach provides greater control over graft dimensions and composition. No single harvesting technique or adjunctive intervention is universally superior. In addition to the harvesting technique and the resulting wound configuration, donor-site morbidity is determined by interactions among patient-related medical factors, palatal anatomy, graft dimensions and composition, and performance of the surgery. Pain and bleeding are the most frequently assessed early outcomes, whereas wound dehiscence, necrosis, infection, persistent sensory disturbances, and symptomatic scarring remain insufficiently quantified. The risk of postoperative morbidity and complications may be reduced through careful medical and anatomical assessment, the use of the minimum effective graft dimensions, atraumatic tissue handling, preservation of adequately vascularized residual tissues, effective hemostasis with appropriate wound protection, and easy-to-follow postoperative instructions for patients. Standardized endpoints, outcome measures, assessment intervals, and CTG-specific risk-assessment tools are needed to improve the comparability of evidence and guide clinical decision-making.

paper_title: The Questions Patients Do Not Ask: A Narrative Review of the Hidden Agenda in Psychiatric Consultations
paper_abstract: Background: Patients frequently leave consultations with concerns, expectations and questions they never voice. This “hidden agenda” carries particular weight in psychiatry, where stigma, power asymmetry, fear of coercion and the illness itself may suppress disclosure. Methods: This narrative review synthesised conversation-analytic, observational, qualitative and interventional studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses on agenda-setting, patient expectations, question-asking, shared decision-making and communication in medical and psychiatric consultations. Seminal and replicated findings were prioritised, and reporting followed the SANRA criteria for narrative reviews. Results: Clinicians often fail to elicit or complete the patient’s agenda, interrupting opening statements within seconds. Unvoiced concerns underlie misunderstandings, unwanted prescriptions, non-adherence and dissatisfaction. In psychiatric settings, many patients ask no questions, patients with psychosis struggle to raise the content of their experiences, and suicidal ideation is concealed chiefly for fear of involuntary hospitalisation. Barriers operate at interactional, psychological, sociocultural and illness-specific levels, and may be amplified in Indian practice by brief consultations and family-mediated decision-making. Clinician agenda-setting skills, question prompt lists, pre-consultation coaching and shared decision-making programmes adapted for severe mental illness measurably increase patient participation. Conclusions: The questions patients do not ask are often those that most need answers. Eliciting and negotiating the hidden agenda should be regarded as a core, teachable competency of psychiatric practice, supported by communication training, patient preparation tools and consultation structures that make unspoken concerns speakable.

paper_title: Beyond Conventional Reservoirs: A Mechanistic Review of CO₂ Storage in Basalt and Granite
paper_abstract: Basalt and granite offer complementary opportunities for geological CO2 storage where conventional sedimentary reservoirs are limited or permanent mineral trapping and geothermal integration are priorities. This review examines how mineralogy, pore and fracture architecture and fluid-rock reactions control storage performance in these crystalline reservoirs. Basalt contains reactive olivine, pyroxene, plagioclase and volcanic glass that release Ca2+, Mg2+ and Fe2+, supporting carbonate precipitation. Field projects including CarbFix and Wallula demonstrate its potential for rapid mineralization. Granite is less reactive and has low primary porosity, making storage dependent largely on natural or engineered fractures. Feldspar alteration and integration with Enhanced Geothermal Systems may nevertheless support combined CO2 storage and heat extraction. In both lithologies, dissolution and secondary precipitation modify porosity, permeability and injectivity, creating a tradeoff between mineral trapping and sustained fluid flow. Laboratory experiments, field demonstrations and reactive transport models are evaluated to identify the principal controls on mineralization and reservoir performance. Key research needs include improved laboratory-to-field scaling, coupled hydrochemical and geomechanical modeling and dedicated granite field validation. Basalt and granite should therefore be considered complementary components of a diversified geological carbon storage portfolio.

paper_title: Paying for Marriage in a Squeezed Market: A Thematic Review of Research on Bride Price and Marriage Squeeze in China, 1990–2026
paper_abstract: Bride price (caili) has become one of the most debated features of contemporary Chinese marriage. Rising payments, a surplus of unmarried men, and public controversy over the "commodification" of marriage have generated a large and multidisciplinary literature. This paper reviews 46 publications from 1990 to 2026 drawn from demography, economics, sociology, gender studies, law and media studies. The literature is organized into five themes: (1) demographic foundations of the marriage squeeze; (2) economic explanations and consequences of marriage payments; (3) gender, family and women's position; (4) historical and cultural transformation of marriage customs; and (5) rural governance, law and public discourse. The review shows that most explanations converge on a market logic in which sex-ratio imbalance and competition for brides raise payments, while newer work emphasizes women's agency, class and regional variation, and the moral politics of bride price. Gaps remain in causal identification, urban–rural and regional comparison, men's experiences, and evaluation of policy interventions. A research agenda is proposed.

paper_title: LED Spectral Composition and Daily Light Integral for Energy-Efficient Basil Production in Plant Factory Systems: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: The demand for year-round production of high-quality crops has increased interest in plant factories with artificial lighting (PFALs). However, artificial lighting is a major energy demand in indoor production. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on the effects of LED spectral composition, photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD), photoperiod, and daily light integral (DLI) on basil (Ocimum basilicum L.). The review focused on growth, quality, and energy-use efficiency. The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Sixty peer-reviewed studies were included from Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Red-blue and broadband spectra supported high biomass production. Blue, ultraviolet, and selected far-red treatments modified phytochemical, essential oil, morphological, and quality traits. These responses varied with cultivar and lighting conditions. DLI influenced biomass and light-use efficiency. However, similar DLI values produced different responses when PPFD and photoperiod differed. Higher light inputs also did not consistently produce proportional gains in biomass or energy-use efficiency. Overall, efficient basil production requires coordinated management of spectrum, PPFD, DLI, photoperiod, cultivar, and production stage. An integrated lighting optimization framework is proposed to balance crop productivity, quality, and energy-use efficiency in PFALs.

paper_title: Prognostic Determinants and Scoring Systems in Fournier Gangrene: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background: Fournier’s gangrene (FG) is a rapidly progressive necrotizing soft-tissue infection associated with substantial mortality despite modern surgical, antimicrobial, and critical-care management. Objective: To synthesize the evidence supporting clinical determinants, FG-specific severity scores, LRINEC, inflammatory biomarkers, general critical-care and comorbidity instruments, and emerging mortality indices in FG. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for publications from 1980 to 2026 using terms related to FG, necrotizing fasciitis, mortality prediction, FGSI, UFGSI, SFGSI, LRINEC, NLR, SOFA/qSOFA, NEWS2, APACHE, Charlson indices, Surgical Apgar Score, FGMI, and FGMI-2P. Original derivation studies, validation cohorts, comparative studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses were prioritized. Diagnostic instruments were considered separately from mortality-prediction tools, and retained quantitative claims were checked against their cited primary sources. Results: Large syntheses place FG mortality at approximately 16–20%, with one 25-year review reporting 19.8% mortality among 6,152 cases and no significant temporal improvement [8]. FGSI, UFGSI, and SFGSI remain the best-established FG-specific composite scores; a 40-study meta-analysis reported pooled AUCs of 0.90, 0.94, and 0.84, respectively [21]. LRINEC was developed for diagnosis of necrotizing fasciitis and performs less consistently for mortality prediction in FG [19,20,25,27]. NLR is associated with mortality at thresholds of ≥8 and ≥10 but is best regarded as an adjunct rather than a stand-alone score [73]. CCI/ACCI, SOFA/qSOFA, NEWS2, and APACHE II add information on comorbidity and systemic severity, whereas FGMI and FGMI-2P are promising newer indices requiring further external validation [20,27,28,49,54,60]. Conclusions: Prognostic assessment in FG is best approached as multidimensional. FG-specific scores should be interpreted together with organ dysfunction, comorbidity burden, and inflammatory/nutritional markers. No prognostic score should delay resuscitation, broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy, or urgent surgical source control.

paper_title: Artificial Intelligence in Vehicular Networks: A Comprehensive Review of Security Challenges and Defenses
paper_abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into vehicular networks has fundamentally transformed intelligent transportation systems, enabling autonomous driving, cooperative perception, and real-time traffic management. However, this convergence has simultaneously expanded the security attack surface, creating novel vulnerabilities that traditional cryptographic defenses alone cannot address. This comprehensive review examines the intersection of AI, vehicular networks, and security, providing a systematic analysis of emerging threats and defense mechanisms. We first establish the architectural foundations of modern vehicular networks, tracing the evolution from Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) to the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) and AI-native V2X systems. We then present a multi-layered threat taxonomy encompassing traditional protocol-level attacks and AI-specific vulnerabilities, including adversarial examples, data poisoning, model inversion, and Byzantine attacks in federated learning environments. Our analysis of defense mechanisms covers machine learning-based intrusion detection systems, blockchain-assisted trust management, federated learning with privacy preservation, and adversarial robustness techniques. We identify critical research gaps, particularly the disconnection between theoretical attack demonstrations and real-world validation, the tension between privacy preservation and detection efficacy, and the unresolved challenge of securing distributed learning under non-IID vehicular data distributions. The review concludes by proposing an integrated security framework that addresses these challenges through explainable AI, adaptive defense mechanisms, and safety-certifiable architectures for next-generation vehicular systems.

paper_title: From Routing Signals to Selective Review: Visual regrounding in MoE VLMs
paper_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) may accept false visual premises, answering questions about a target object's color, count, location, or state even when it is absent. We call this reliability-critical behavior a target-absence grounding failure. Existing visual-grounding detectors primarily rely on generated responses, hidden states, or uncertainty measures. We present the first framework to leverage internal routing decisions in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) VLMs to detect target absence before generation and guide selective correction. We extract target-token routing probabilities from Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct and Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, train a separate L2-regularized linear detector for each model, and use its predictions to selectively invoke a target-aware review prompt. Using routing alone, the Qwen and Gemma detectors achieve ROC-AUCs of 0.9988 and 0.9956 on GQA-Inpaint and retain 0.8095 and 0.7781 on the external OBER dataset, respectively. The resulting routing-gated policy improves end-to-end accuracy on GQA-Inpaint and OBER by +22.25% and +12.17% for Qwen, and by +13.42% and +1.39% for Gemma, without modifying model weights. Further analysis shows that the signal is localized to the target-object token, emerges in early MoE layers, and is distributed across partially substitutable experts. Although cross-dataset threshold shifts require recalibration, false-positive review causes limited harm overall, suggesting that intervention risk can be controlled through joint selection of the detector threshold and review prompt. Overall, we show that routing probabilities alone preserve actionable information about visual perception, allowing computation already produced by an MoE VLM to support low-cost detection and selective visual regrounding.

paper_title: CRJudgeBench: Can AI Detect Plausible but Invalid Code Reviews?
paper_abstract: Large language models can generate plausible code-review comments, but such comments may contain technically incorrect claims that mislead developers. We study technical trustworthiness judgment: determining whether a review comment's core technical claims are correct and applicable to the reviewed code in its repository context. Existing code-review benchmarks primarily evaluate review generation, issue discovery, or general comment quality, but do not directly assess whether an agent can determine the technical trustworthy of an individual review comment. To fill this gap, we introduce CRJudgeBench, a benchmark of 1199 instances constructed from real pull requests and expert-verified perturbations, covering both trustworthy and plausible but untrustworthy comments. We further present Sentinel, a repository-grounded agentic judge that actively gathers code evidence to verify review comments before making judgments. Starting from Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, Sentinel is trained on the CRJudgeBench training split through iterative action-level learning from a privileged teacher. On the 359-instance CRJudgeBench test set, Sentinel achieves 76.60\% accuracy, outperforming GLM-5.3 by 6.13 percentage points and its base model by 19.78 points. These results show that even state-of-the-art general-purpose LLMs struggle to identify untrustworthy comments, while iterative action-level learning substantially improves the accuracy of repository-grounded trustworthiness judgments. Our dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/dcloud347/CRJudgeBenchmark
comments: 26 pages, 5 figures, and 14 tables. Under review at ICLR 2027. Dataset available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/dcloud347/CRJudgeBenchmark

paper_title: Breaking the Illusion of Review Reliability under Static Evaluation: SCOPE Fuzzing for LLM-based Scientific Reviewers
paper_abstract: The rapid growth of submissions and reviewing workload has accelerated the use of large language models (LLMs) in peer review. Prior studies suggest that LLM-based reviewers can penalize content perturbations, such as overclaiming, indicating a certain degree of reliability. Yet these conclusions are largely based on a narrow set of perturbation strategies instantiated with static templates, providing limited evidence of actual reliability. In this paper, we construct a three-level evaluation framework covering perturbations to surface presentation, argumentative logic, and value judgment. Experiments on representative LLM-based reviewers reveal two limitations of static evaluation: stratified vulnerability, where perturbation effects depend on whether the paper's original review score is high or low, and perturbation undercoverage, where a single template misses vulnerabilities exposed by diverse realizations. To address these limitations, we propose SCOPE-Fuzzer, a strategy-aware fuzzer that combines feedback-driven strategy selection with adaptive mutation of paper content. By iteratively probing reviewers with dynamic perturbations, SCOPE-Fuzzer consistently uncovers vulnerabilities overlooked by static evaluation and other baselines.

paper_title: Cross-Organizational SysML Model Integration: A Survey of Challenges and AI-Supported Tasks
paper_abstract: Cross-organizational collaboration is widely regarded as a key promise of SysML-based Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), yet practitioners still face persistent challenges when exchanging and integrating system models. In parallel, Large Language Models (LLMs) raise expectations for AI-assisted model understanding and integration, while reliability and required human oversight continue to pose challenges. This paper reports the results of an online questionnaire survey with 29 MBSE stakeholders involved in cross-organizational collaboration. Respondents rated eight predefined integration challenge categories and six AI-supported task types on five-point Likert scales. The results indicate that stakeholders perceive model integration as a multi-dimensional alignment problem across semantics, behavior, traceability, and exchange interoperability. These perceptions vary by organizational role and frequency of integration involvement. AI is rated highly useful for analysis tasks such as semantic structure analysis and inconsistency detection, and respondents predominantly prefer human-in-the-loop use with mandatory verification. These findings motivate AI support that enhances, rather than replaces, engineering responsibility in SysML-based integration.

paper_title: Community Pharmacies and Health Promotion Services in Nigeria: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background: Pharmacy practice has evolved globally and health promotion is an essential part of modern Pharmacy Practice. Community pharmacies serve as accessible and trusted healthcare providers. Studies on different health promotion activities done in community Pharmacies in Nigeria abound. This review aims to identify health-promotional services offered in community Pharmacies in Nigeria, including studies conducted on health Promotion in community Pharmacies from February 2010 to March 2025, to provide an update on recent developments and emerging trends. Additionally, barriers and recommendations for future research will be captured. Methods: A narrative review of studies was conducted by searching PubMed and Google Scholar to identify health-promoting activities of community Pharmacies in Nigeria. Studies of any design were included if they focused on health Promotion activities in community Pharmacies in Nigeria, published within the study period, and in English. Excluded studies were those that had no full text available. The studies were analyzed narratively.Results: This review selected 19 articles, including 10 Cross-sectional studies, 6 Narrative reviews, and 3 interventional studies. The studies were mostly conducted in Lagos State and Ibadan. Community pharmacies in Nigeria were increasingly involved in health promotion services, including chronic disease management, disease screening, smoking cessation, oral health promotion, mental health, vaccination, and public health responses during emergencies. While they are making significant contributions, there is substantial potential for further engagement, particularly if barriers such as inadequate training, regulatory and policy constraints, and lack of access to patient information are addressed Conclusion: Community pharmacies in Nigeria are increasingly involved in health promotion services. Policy reforms and targeted interventions, modeled on successful international practices, could fully integrate community pharmacies into the healthcare system, improving healthcare delivery and outcomes in Nigeria. Studies on the implementation of strategies and interventions to enhance community Pharmacies' health promotion roles are needed.

paper_title: Prognostic Factors and Treatment Effect Modifier Candidates in Advanced HER2-Mutant NSCLC: A Targeted Literature Review
paper_abstract: Background: The expanding availability of targeted therapies for HER2-mutant non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has led to increased interest in understanding the baseline characteristics of patients that may impact clinical outcomes. This literature review evaluates prognostic factors and treatment effect modifiers in HER2 mutant NSCLC to inform indirect treatment comparison (ITC). Methods: A targeted literature review (TLR) was conducted and reported in accordance with an adapted PRISMA framework. The review included observational studies and clinical trials assessing survival outcomes among adults with advanced HER2-mutant NSCLC, irrespective of prior systemic therapy. Subgroups of interest included age, sex, smoking status, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS), metastatic status, prior treatment history, HER2-mutation subtype, and other clinically relevant baseline characteristics. Searches were conducted in Embase and Medline to identify English‑language publications from January 2019 to 20 December 2025. Results: Based on data from 33 included publications (19 observational studies and 14 publications reporting results from 11 clinical trials), most demographic factors, including age, sex, and smoking status, were not found to be of consistent prognostic or predictive value in HER2-mutant NSCLC patients. However, several disease‑related and molecular characteristics, including ECOG PS, metastatic burden, HER2-mutation subtype (especially the YVMA/Y772_A775dup variant) and co‑mutations (particularly TP53), demonstrated more consistent associations across studies with clinical outcomes. Conclusion: These findings provide structured evidence base for variable selection and sensitivity analyses in ITCs, while underscoring the need for prospective controlled studies capable of formally evaluating treatment heterogeneity in this molecularly distinct population.

paper_title: Positive Psychology as a Strategy for Human Development: A Systematic Review of Interventions, Outcomes, Contexts, and Implementation Conditions
paper_abstract: Introduction: Positive psychology interventions are increasingly used in educational, workplace, and community settings to support well-being, personal growth, resilience, engagement, and other indicators of human development. However, the evidence spans diverse interventions, populations, outcomes, and cultural contexts, and the extent to which positive effects are sustained or transferable remains uncertain.Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, PubMed (MEDLINE), ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2020–2026. COSTAQDA recorded source-level retrieval through OpenAlex (250 retrieved; 14323 available), Crossref (250 retrieved; 27071 available). Where researcher-selected sources did not expose a suitable direct bulk-search connector, COSTAQDA used its OpenAlex/Crossref discovery bridge while preserving the researcher-selected source names in the PRISMA record. The identification run recorded 500 records before cross-source deduplication and 487 unique records after deduplication.Results: The synthesis generated one descriptive theme and six analytical themes. Positive psychology interventions were associated with strengthened personal resources; strengths-based reflection supported identity development and intentional growth; positive emotional climates created pathways to engagement and performance; benefits depended on supportive relationships and enabling environments; cultural and situational fit constrained transferability; implementation required preparation, competence, and ethical safeguards; and the evidence supported promise but not definitive claims about long-term human development. Convergence was strongest for self-efficacy, engagement, resilience, and relational support, while divergent findings concerned emotional coexistence, cultural variation, sustainability, and possible harms.Discussion/Conclusion: Positive psychology interventions show promise as context-dependent strategies for human development, but the evidence does not justify universal or definitive causal claims. Transferable implications favour strengths-based, relational, culturally responsive, and institutionally supported implementation.

paper_title: Student Engagement as a Dynamic and Relational Process: A Critical Review of the Construct and Its Implications for Educational Psychology
paper_abstract: Student engagement has become a central construct in educational psychology because of its association with learning, academic achievement, persistence, school adjustment, and well-being. Despite its relevance, the literature still shows considerable conceptual diversity regarding its definition, dimensions, antecedents, and consequences. This article presents a critical, narrative review of the evolution of the construct, from conceptualizations centered on participation and identification with school to multidimensional models integrating behavioral, emotional, cognitive, and agentic dimensions. Particular attention is given to the relational and contextual nature of engagement, including the roles of teacher support, social relationships, sense of belonging, and well-being. The analysis draws on a line of research developed in Portugal within vocational and secondary education and connects it with classic and contemporary international literature. Recent evidence suggests that the different dimensions of engagement play partially distinct roles: behavioral engagement shows particularly strong associations with achievement, agentic engagement with social support, and emotional engagement with motivation and well-being. It is argued that engagement should not be understood as a stable trait of the student, nor reduced to observable participation, but as a dynamic process that emerges from the interaction between students and educational contexts.

paper_title: Simulating Respondents, Not Single Questions: Coherent Survey Generation with Large Language Models
paper_abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate response distributions in social surveys. Prior work has achieved accurate population-level simulation for individual questions. Real questionnaires, however, ask each respondent a sequence of related questions. A simulated respondent should show coherent preferences across the whole questionnaire, not merely accurate distributions for isolated items. Existing single-item methods cannot accurately reproduce how the same person answers a complete survey. We propose FullRespondent-LLM (FR-LLM), which fine-tunes two specialized LLMs: a marginal model for each item's response distribution and a respondent-level autoregressive model for dependencies across answers. Marginal-Constrained Joint Projection (MCJP) then projects the autoregressive joint distribution onto the set satisfying the item-level marginals learned by the first model. This yields complete questionnaires with realistic cross-item relationships while retaining strong item-level accuracy. On two real-world social survey datasets, FR-LLM more accurately reproduces multi-question response patterns, maintains competitive single-item accuracy, and generalizes better to unseen populations and questions. In a small commercial-survey dataset, we use simulated responses to make pricing and stocking decisions; FR-LLM achieves the highest realized profit.

paper_title: Recent Advances in Agentic Agri-Robotic Phenotyping: A Perspective Review from Fragmented Multimodal Sensing to Unified PhenoAgent Intelligence
paper_abstract: This review examines the evolution of plant phenotyping from conventional manual trait measurement to high-throughput, robotic, and artificial intelligence-driven crop monitoring. Despite significant advances in imaging, autonomous platforms, multimodal sensing, and deep learning, current phenotyping systems remain fragmented across sensing modalities, crop traits, growth stages, environments, and management objectives. We therefore frame phenotyping as an integrated \emph{seed-soil-plant-environment-management} (SSPEM) intelligence problem, where crop performance reflects interactions among seed quality, root-zone conditions, plant development, environmental exposure, and management actions. The review synthesizes conventional, high-throughput, robotic, and AI-driven phenotyping approaches, highlighting their capabilities and persistent limitations in temporal integration, multimodal reasoning, biological interpretation, and actionable decision support. Building on this analysis, we introduce a conceptual PhenoAgent framework that extends phenotyping beyond the estimation of isolated traits to evidence-based crop-state interpretation, uncertainty-aware reasoning, and management-oriented support. The PhenoAgent concept primarily brings together scattered advances in phenotyping to deliver insights ranging from detailed to high-level, such as what is happening in the crop, why it might be occurring, what evidence is missing, and what actions or additional measurements should be considered. We also discuss challenges in dataset scarcity, annotation, benchmarking, model generalization, and explainability. By linking multimodal phenotyping with agentic AI and closed-loop decision support, this review outlines a path to interpretable, scalable, and deployment-oriented crop intelligence.

paper_title: What Does a Skill Actually Do? Estimands and Evaluation Validity for Tool and Skill Use in LLM Agents: A Critical Review
paper_abstract: Reported improvements from tools and reusable skills in large language model agents refer to different comparisons. This critical narrative review examines what these evaluations estimate and which conclusions their designs support. The review checks the roles of one hundred cited papers and extracts focal evaluation designs in detail from thirty-five studies. Targeted readings of thirty-five additional published or accepted studies broaden coverage of tool creation, memory, interactive benchmarks, reliability, and risk. Designs are characterized by treatment contrast, target population, outcome, budget constraint, summary measure, and identification assumptions. Analytic decompositions and counterexamples show that pairing runs on the same task does not itself identify an invocation effect when evaluation conditions on a trigger within the treated run. Paired gain and regression counts describe discordance under the coupling protocol rather than the share of tasks whose expected outcomes worsen. Total effects of deploying a module answer a different question from efficiency under a common budget. Comparisons across studies distinguish curated skill provision from retriever replacement, task populations from triggered subsets, and preparation costs from marginal usage costs. Publication status and reading depth are recorded. The review provides a methodological synthesis and a reporting checklist to help align claims about tools and skills with the comparisons their evaluation designs support.
comments: 50 pages; critical narrative review. Expanded literature coverage and study-level evidence tables; clarified evaluation estimands and methodological analyses; revised figures and text

paper_title: EEG-Based Motor Imagery BCI Algorithms and Technologies: A Review
paper_abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have emerged as transformative technologies that enable direct communication between the brain and external devices. Among various BCI paradigms, EEG-based motor imagery (MI) has gained prominence due to its simplicity, non-invasiveness, and potential to restore motor function and facilitate rehabilitation for patients with motor impairments. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the most practical processing algorithms developed over the past decade for decoding brain sensorimotor cortex signals. Specifically, this paper discusses the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-based algorithms, particularly machine learning and deep learning techniques, and their contributions to improving the performance and efficiency of MI-BCI systems in detail. Furthermore, the paper reviews state-of-the-art hardware platforms and emerging converging technologies, including system-on-chip (SoC) architectures, application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), wearable devices, the Internet of Things (IoT), and augmented/virtual reality (AR/VR), and discusses their integration with advanced signal processing algorithms to enable next-generation MI-BCI systems. By highlighting current achievements of EEG-based MI-BCI technology and predicting future research directions that could further enhance real-time capabilities, this paper aims to provide valuable insights for researchers and practitioners, fostering innovation in high-performance EEG-based MI-BCI systems.

paper_title: Can Open-Weight Large Language Models (LLMs) Simulate Human Survey Populations? A Cross-Instrument Calibration Study
paper_abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate synthetic survey respondents and digital twins of real people, but whether their output preserves real human statistical structure, rather than surface plausibility, remains unresolved, and most existing evidence comes from proprietary models rather than open-weight ones. We evaluate three open-weight LLM families on a cross-instrument calibration task: conditioning personas on real respondents' verbatim answers to one psychometric instrument and measuring them on a second, construct-distance-controlled instrument, checked against a 2,058-person human panel. Across a 139-pair grid, the simulated cross-instrument correlation tracks the real human correlation at r = 0.70 - 0.73 in every model, driven mainly by correct sign rather than precise magnitude and concentrated in pairs of moderate construct distance. A correlation of this magnitude, obtained from untuned open-weight models conditioned only on individual-level survey data, is a substantively encouraging result for LLM-based behavioral simulation and digital-twin applications: specific model families and releases already reproduce a meaningful share of real human cross-instrument structure without any fine-tuning. This capability does not, however, improve monotonically across model releases: on a matched panel, the newest of three tested Llama releases performs worst on two of three headline metrics, so realizing its promise in practice requires release-specific, distance-aware verification rather than a one-time benchmark.

paper_title: What Can a Leaderboard Certify? Compositional Controllability for Fair Evaluation and Training of Biomedical Literature-Review Agents
paper_abstract: Leaderboards rank long-horizon agents by their final outputs. Yet a higher score alone does not establish whether two systems are comparable or which stage accounts for the difference. Unequal evidence, inputs, or budgets can affect scores, and statistical corrections do not remove this mismatch. We introduce compositional controllability to address these questions. A comparison window covers one stage, several stages, or the whole agent. Our central result bounds the gap between observed and controlled score differences using only nuisance outside the window. This yields an admissibility test applied before scores are inspected. Inadmissible comparisons are refused. For admissible pairs, an ordering is certified only when the score gap exceeds the combined sampling and nuisance radii; otherwise, it remains undecided. These decisions give each system a rank interval. We introduce BioLitBench, a benchmark of 2,042 biomedical articles represented as structured claim graphs. Among seven published pipelines, a conventional statistical analysis declares a winner in 14 of 21 pairwise comparisons. Yet the top-ranked system alone received the target review's bibliography. To isolate pipeline performance, our test requires matched inputs and a fixed backbone model. It refuses 11 of the 21 comparisons, including every comparison involving the top-ranked system. Seven of the 14 conventional conclusions fall within these refused pairs. The same comparison windows support stage-level training. We train SCRIBE on Qwen3.8-27B using rewards measured at each stage's exit. Under matched evidence, SCRIBE achieves a certified rank interval of [1,2], with certified advantages over all evaluated published pipelines and the evaluated Claude and OpenAI agents. Under same pool, SCRIBE matches the strongest published retriever and is certified above three published pipelines.
comments: 33 pages, 1 figure, 18 tables. Zhaowei Han, Xiang Zhang, and Lingxiao Guan contributed equally. Code: https://github.com/shawnzhg/LitReview-SCRIBE

paper_title: Educational and Counseling Competencies of Midwives in the Prevention of Sexually Transmitted Infections Across a Woman’s Life Course: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) remain a significant public health challenge due to dynamic epidemiological and behavioral shifts. The diversity of pathogens necessitates complex strategies for screening, diagnosis, and prevention, supported by health education and counseling to mitigate risky sexual behaviors. This narrative review aims to systematize and analyze the educational and counseling competencies of midwives in the prevention of sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) across the distinct stages of a woman's life course. The professional role of the midwife in STI prevention is grounded in clinical knowledge and counseling skills that support women in maintaining optimal sexual and reproductive health. During puberty, age-appropriate history-taking and sensitive communication facilitate the provision of critical information regarding STIs, HPV, and early prophylaxis. Furthermore, STI prevention is vital for ensuring safe pregnancy and childbirth outcomes, with midwifery competencies directly influencing the development of health literacy, informed sexual behavior, and responsible health practices among young people. In early reproductive age, clinical counseling fosters sustainable health habits and responsible attitudes, thereby preserving vital reproductive functions. Particular emphasis is placed on regular prophylactic gynecological check-ups, which enable the early identification of infections and functional anomalies, supporting long-term gynecological well-being. Ultimately, comprehensive care for women of reproductive age incorporates structured professional support to sustain sexual health and strengthen community-based infection prevention.

paper_title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Manufacturing and Materials Processing: A Review of Engineering Validation and Decision Support
paper_abstract: Machine-learning predictions are used to assess material properties, monitor manufacturing processes and support inspection and maintenance. Their engineering value depends on whether the information used by a model can be examined and related to the physical task. This narrative review considers interpretable models, feature attribution, response plots, visual explanations and constrained counterfactuals in manufacturing and materials processing. It distinguishes predictive performance from explanation fidelity, physical evidence and decision usefulness. Selected applications illustrate these differences: process–property modelling in additive manufacturing, acoustic monitoring, tool-condition assessment, ultrasonic defect sizing and uncertainty in production processes. A comparison of these examples shows why the prediction target; data representation and validation procedure must be stated before explanation results are interpreted. The review proposes four categories of explanation use—descriptive, diagnostic, prescriptive and governed—and identifies the additional evidence required for each. The main methodological concerns are dependent inputs, unrealistic perturbations, non-independent observations and changes in the model or operating conditions. Explanation methods can help examine a model and guide further investigation, but process changes require separate checks of feasibility and physical consequences. The narrative selection does not establish the prevalence of individual methods across the field.

paper_title: Sugar Consumption and Health Outcomes: Implications for Nursing Education, Clinical Practice, and Health Policy: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Background: Excessive sugar consumption is a major contributor to chronic diseases including obesity, type 2 diabetes, dental caries, and mental health disorders. International evidence highlights the need to integrate nutrition and lifestyle education into nursing curricula. In Albania, where non-communicable diseases are rising, nursing education and clinical practice must adapt to address these challenges. Aim: This scoping review aimed to map recent evidence on sugar consumption, health outcomes, and policy interventions, and to explore how these can be integrated into nursing education and practice in Albania. Methods: Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, six databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, ERIC, Academic Search Premier, PsycINFO) were searched for studies published between January 2021 and June 2026. Inclusion criteria were peer-reviewed articles in English addressing sugar consumption, health outcomes, or policy frameworks relevant to nursing education. Data extraction was performed using a structured template and analyzed through inductive thematic analysis. Results: Three dimensions emerged: ● Contextual: System-level interventions such as taxation, labeling, and public health campaigns support healthier choices. ● Social: Cultural norms, family practices, and peer influences shape sugar consumption, requiring community-based interventions. ● Individual: Sugar intake is linked to chronic disease, dental health, and mental well-being, highlighting the need for counseling and behavioral support. Rising rates of obesity and diabetes at QSUT underscore the urgency of integrating these dimensions into nursing curricula. Conclusion: Sugar consumption poses a multidimensional challenge requiring contextual, social, and individual responses. Nursing education at University Aldent should incorporate policy literacy, community engagement, and counseling skills. Collaboration between QSUT, academic institutions, and public health authorities is essential to strengthen Albania’s response to sugar-related diseases.

paper_title: Gut Microbiome, Blood–Brain Barrier, and Psychiatric Disease: A Translational Review of Microbial Control of Neurovascular Function
paper_abstract: Background: The gut microbiota regulates brain function through metabolite, immune, and neural signaling, and emerging evidence identifies the blood–brain barrier (BBB), gatekeeper of the neurovascular unit, as a principal target of this influence. BBB disruption is increasingly recognized in major psychiatric disorders, suggesting microbiota-driven neurovascular change contributes to neuroinflammation in depression and schizophrenia. Objective: To synthesize evidence that gut microorganisms and metabolites regulate BBB structure and function, link these mechanisms to psychiatric pathophysiology, and evaluate microbiota-targeted interventions acting through the neurovascular axis. Methods: Narrative review of preclinical, mechanistic, and clinical literature, including germ-free and antibiotic-depletion models, in vitro BBB models, case-control microbiome studies, barrier-dysfunction biomarkers, and randomized trials of probiotics and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). Results: Germ-free mice show increased BBB permeability with reduced occludin and claudin-5, reversible by bacterial colonization and short-chain fatty acids such as butyrate and propionate, acting via G-protein-coupled receptors, histone deacetylase inhibition, and NF-κB/Nrf2 signaling; trimethylamine-N-oxide and endotoxins instead promote barrier loss. The microbiota drives sex- and time-dependent microglial maturation, and stress-induced gut hyperpermeability with endotoxin translocation links to systemic inflammation and BBB compromise. Human studies show reduced claudin-5 in the nucleus accumbens and hippocampus in depression and schizophrenia, elevated S100B, and dysbiotic signatures with depleted butyrate-producing taxa. Probiotic trials show modest improvement; FMT remains experimental with unresolved durability. Conclusions: Microbial control of neurovascular function is a plausible, mechanistically rich pathway linking gut to psychiatric disease. Translation requires standardized methodology, prospective causal designs, sex-aware analysis, and biomarker-guided trials targeting the BBB as an endpoint.

paper_title: Influence of the ADRB2 Gene on Sporting Ability and the Human Body: A Literature Review
paper_abstract: This review assesses the influence of ADRB2 (beta-2 adrenergic receptor) gene polymorphisms on athletic performance and physiological function in humans.
